reason: Nothing that arrived in the three sessions since this leg filled on 2026-09-16 is new information, and everything that did arrive confirms the book. The 9/16 FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% with 'inflation remains elevated' and language about a 'timelier return' to 2% - that is the exact regime this book was rebuilt for last week (hard-asset dividend aristocrats over expensive low-yield bond proxies), and it was already in my entry prices. Oil is still doing the work: WTI $100.30, +18.9% on the month and +60.7% on the year, with Chevron's CEO publicly warning on global supply and both majors negotiating a return to Venezuela. The three-session dip below $100 is the Saudi pipeline risk premium deflating, not the structural bid going away, and CVX/XOM/EPD already carry -12%/-12%/-10% stops to define that risk for me. The rest of the book is intact leg by leg: USB is directly levered to the hike and moved its prime rate to 7.00% in mid-September, trading at 12x with a 3.6% yield and ~17% consensus upside; EPD (+2.10%) is the best mark in the book on record Q2 EBITDA and export volumes at a 5.76% distribution yield; ABBV has Phase 3 wins on atogepant and etentamig plus the Apogee close; the SCHD core is +27% YTD total return as money rotates toward established dividend payers. Every mark sits between -0.96% and +2.10% - there is no thesis break anywhere to react to. Against that, this is already leg 8 in nine weeks. Re-registering eight legs pays 2bps a side plus SEC/TAF and, more importantly, re-bases every entry fill and therefore every stop-loss level to the 9/21 close, throwing away the risk framework I set three days ago in exchange for a view I have not actually changed. The one thing I did find worth flagging for next week rather than trading on today: JNJ at a 1.99% yield, 31x trailing earnings and ~3% consensus upside is now the weakest dividend-growth math in the book and the leg most like the expensive defensive this strategy exists to avoid - if the DePuy Synthes divestiture talks resolve or it stalls again while rates hold at 4%, that 6% is the funding source for the next energy or financials add. A 6-point swap is not worth resetting the whole book's fills for now. Cash at 12% is also being paid properly at 4% APY against a 4% funds rate, so there is no penalty for waiting.
